label: ex:hydrogen-derived-nf
title: Hydrogen: full normal form from pair production
html:
Example. Hydrogen \mathcal{A}(1,0) derived from 3 \times \gamma\gamma pair production.

Derivation chain

  3(\gamma\gamma) \xrightarrow{\text{pair prod.}} (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2, \mathfrak{d}_3) + (\bar{\mathfrak{u}}_1, \bar{\mathfrak{u}}_2, \bar{\mathfrak{d}}_3) \xrightarrow{\mathcal{B}_3} \xrightarrow{\text{gluon } \sigma_0^2} \mathfrak{p} \xrightarrow{\sigma_0} \mathfrak{p} \oplus T_{2,3} = \mathcal{A}(1,0)

Step 1. Three 4-term \gamma\gamma collisions produce three quark-antiquark pairs. Step 2. The operator \mathcal{B}_3 confines the three quarks (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2, \mathfrak{d}_3). Step 2b. The LP-derived gluon stabilises the confined state. This yields the proton normal form with \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p}) \approx +0.986. Step 3. The proton Hopf-links to the electron via the electromagnetic crossing \sigma_0:

  \mathcal{A}(1,0) = \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{p} \cdot \sigma_0 \cdot e^-).

Hydrogen NF

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathcal{A}(1,0)) = +0.090\gamma + 1.018\sigma_0 - 0.024\sigma_1 + 0.213 L_+ + 0.112 L_- + 0.080 e^-.
  \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{A}(1,0)) \approx +1.489

The e^- coefficient flips from -0.043 (unbound proton) to +0.080 (hydrogen atom). The Hopf linking with the electron satisfies the proton's trefoil deficit. The bound atom has e^- > 0, closing the beta decay channel. The only remaining deficit is \sigma_1 = -0.024. This reflects the incomplete 1s^1 shell. Hydrogen has one electron rather than the closed-shell pair of helium.
